tooltip.nomadic_herbs.poultice.tooltip: Can be chewed into a poultice.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.goldenrod.tooltip: Goldenrod is a herb used for treating open wounds, helping prevent infection.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.horse_mint.tooltip: Can be applied to wounds to prevent infection, or eaten to treat respiratory ailments when dried.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.goldenrod_paste.to: Treats open wounds, helping prevent infection. This poultice should be applied directly on the wound after bleeding has stopped.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.elderberry.tooltip: Eaten to treat mild fever and colds.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.catmint.tooltip: Can be used to help with congestion, as well as one of the main remedies for greencough, when breathed in or eaten. Can also be used to relax and calm cats.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.yarrow.tooltip: Excellent for fresh wounds and one of the most important battlefield herbs by applying pieces of yarrow to the wound.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.echinacea.tooltip: Used to support the body's response to infection.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.white_sagebrush.to: Crushed leaves clean wounds and repel insects, when sprinkled over a cat.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.ribwort_paste.tool: Applied to skin for splinters, stings, and minor infections.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.sundrops_paste.too: Used for inflammation and skin ailments, such as bruising, or skin irritation.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.boneset.tooltip: Eaten by a cat, it is the most respected fever remedy in The Basin. Highly effective.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.marsh_mallow.toolt: Can be turned into thick, soothing roots that produce a sap.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.marsh_mallow_roots: Produces a sap that coats irritated tissue.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.calamus.tooltip: Used to soothe nausea and upset stomach.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.jewelweed.tooltip: Applying the sap relieves skin irritation and insect bites.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.winterbloom.toolti: Mixing the leaves with water makes an excellent antimicrobial wash that can also reduce swelling.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.winterbloom_leaf.t: Makes an excellent antimicrobial wash when combined with water that can also reduce swelling.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.bulrush.tooltip: Can be stripped into fluff and roots.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.bulrush_fluff.tool: Soft seed fluff that can pad wounds or nests.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.bulrush_roots.tool: While not very appetizing, these roots are edible during famine.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.goldenseal.tooltip: Chewed into a poultice and applied to wounds, its a powerful remedy to serious infected wounds.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.goldenseal_paste.t: A powerful remedy to seriously-infected wounds.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.arnica.tooltip: Applied externally to reduce swelling and bruising after falls or difficult hunts. Never eaten.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.rattleweed.tooltip: Eaten to reduce aches and severe muscle pain.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.usnea.tooltip: Makes a cat tired and relaxes muscles. Used as a powerful temporary sedative.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.juniper.tooltip: Used as a mildly effective antiseptic.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.death_camas.toolti: Causes vomiting, weakness, slowed heartbeat, and can be fatal.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.larkspur.tooltip: Its beautiful blue-purple flowers hide potent alkaloids that affect the nervous system.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.nightshade.tooltip: Berries and foliage may cause stomach upset, confusion, weakness, and, in larger amounts, more severe neurological symptoms.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.poison_ivy.tooltip: Not deadly, but contact with the oils causes painful itching and blistering. Can be treated with Jewelweed.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.devils_trumpet.too: Highly toxic plant that affects the nervous system, causing confusion, dilated pupils, and dangerous hallucinations.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.pokeweed.tooltip: Young shoots and mature plants are highly toxic. When eaten, it can cause stomach illness and eventual death if not treated.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.pine_resin.tooltip: Sticky resin forms a protective barrier over deep cuts and helps prevent contamination.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.moss.tooltip: Used to carry water to cats who can't travel far to drink, as well as soak up blood from wounds.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.cobweb.tooltip: Used to wrap and cover wounds.
tooltip.nomadic_herbs.white_willow.toolt: Can be used as a mild pain relief, and to soothe fevers. This herb is digestible and should be eaten for treatment.
